title: Возвращение старого официанта  (Return of the Former Waiter)

segments.t: At Claude Monet, Max muses on the strange laws of the universe that bring people from the past back into our lives. Right on cue, handsome former waiter Ilya walks into the kitchen and greets the veterans while waiting to ask Vika for his old job back.
Не знаю, по каким законам вселенная это работает.
Возвращается жизнь, которую ты мог потерять.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
Не знаю, по каким законам вселенная это работает.
'I do not know by what laws of the universe this works.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'know' to negate the statement. Vika answers right away.
'Just as it seemed to you.' The grammar packs 'how' and 'to seem' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Возвращается жизнь, которую ты мог потерять.
'The life you could have lost comes back to you.' The meaning hinges on 'comes back' working together with 'to lose' in spoken Russian.
'But sometimes a return happens.' Notice how Russian expresses 'but' and 'return' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'Are you a new guy here or what?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'really'.
'Here you go!' The grammar packs 'and' and 'there you go' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Senya, how is the fricassee coming along.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Senya' and finishing on 'readiness'. Vika answers right away.
'Wait, who is that?' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'who' in spoken Russian.
'He used to work here as a waiter.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'before' and finishing on 'worked'.
'He was almost like a son to me.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'there was' places the action in the masculine past tense. Vika answers right away.
'Not like you.' The grammar packs 'not' and 'you' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Will Viktoriya Sergeyevna take me back?' Senya brings out the contrast between 'Viktoriya' and 'Sergeyevna' in a few short words.
'Ever since you left.' The meaning hinges on 'how' working together with 'left' in spoken Russian. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Не знаю, по каким законам вселенная это работает.
Возвращается жизнь, которую ты мог потерять.
When you watch Scene 1 of Episode 14, listen out for the exchange around return of the former waiter — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
